issues.description: Identifier naming mismatch: the global framebuffer symbol is referred to as 'display_start' in the problem statement and the template, but the solution declares the buffer as 'screen_buffer' while still referencing 'display_start' in code. Problem statement: refers to 'display_start' as the base address for the screen buffer. Template (pixel.asm): defines 'display_start' in .bss. Solution (pixel.asm): declares 'screen_buffer' in .bss (line 5) but uses 'display_start' in instructions (lines 29 and 94). This will produce an undefined symbol at assembly/link time and confuses students about which global name to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the framebuffer symbol name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the declaration in the solution from 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start', or change all uses of 'display_start' in the solution to 'screen_buffer'. Also update the problem statement/template if you intentionally prefer the alternate name. Ensure the final name matches in problem_statement.md, template/pixel.asm, and solution/pixel.asm so the code assembles and students are not confused.

issues.description: Concept: the base address of the framebuffer / screen memory. The problem statement and the template declare and refer to this base as 'display_start' (problem_statement.md: 'display_start'; template_repository/pixel.asm: declaration 'display_start RESB 8294400' at line 21). The solution's .bss declares the buffer as 'screen_buffer' (solution_repository/pixel.asm: 'screen_buffer RESB 8294400' at line 5) but the solution code still references 'display_start' (solution_repository/pixel.asm: references at line 29). This leads to two issues: (1) a cross-artifact naming mismatch between 'display_start' (problem + template) and 'screen_buffer' (solution declaration), making it harder for students to map the required identifier to the implementation; (2) an internal inconsistency in the solution (declares 'screen_buffer' but references 'display_start') that would break assembly and confuse students trying to read or run the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier for the framebuffer base consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's 'screen_buffer' declaration to 'display_start' (change 'screen_buffer RESB 8294400' to 'display_start RESB 8294400' in solution_repository/pixel.asm) and keep all existing references to 'display_start'. Alternatively, update the template and problem statement to use 'screen_buffer' everywhere. Ensure the declaration and all uses in the solution file match exactly so the code assembles and students can clearly map the requirement to the variable.
